entry.title: a short note about iconography
entry.content:
I keep coming back to iconography, so here are the notes I wish I had earlier.

why it matters

Iconography shows up across design work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Optimise for the reader who shows up six months from now with no context.
  • Prefer the obvious solution; clever costs interest forever.
  • Start with the smallest thing that works, then make it boring on purpose.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

entry.title: iconography, revisited
entry.content:
Short post: iconography is one of those things that looks simple until it isn’t.

why it matters

Iconography shows up across design work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • If it is hard to test, that is the design telling you something.
  • Write it down once, link to it everywhere.
  • Measure before you change anything; intuition is a poor profiler.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

entry.title: thinking about iconography
entry.content:
Every few months iconography bites me again. This is what finally stuck.

why it matters

Iconography shows up across design work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Name it after what it does, not after how it does it.
  • Prefer the obvious solution; clever costs interest forever.
  • Make the default path the correct path so nobody has to remember the rule.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.
